mechanism: The University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (headline UMCSENT) is a survey of household economic optimism. Rising sentiment tends to precede stronger spending and risk-on equity conditions; falling sentiment precedes retrenchment.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time UMCSENT vintages), the rule selected on in-sample data uses zscore_60m / T_roll_p50 at L8 (IS Sharpe 0.76); held-out OOS Sharpe 0.71 versus buy-and-hold SPY 0.95.
caveats: The strategy is search-selected and needs a frozen-rule holdout confirmation.
UMCSENT is rarely revised after its final monthly reading, so the as-known-at-the-time and revised tracks differ mainly through release timing and the shorter vintage archive.
The test window was seen by the previously published run, so it is not a frozen hold-out.
narrative_summary: Headline U. Michigan consumer sentiment is tested as a procyclical sentiment overlay for SPY. Compare with umcsent_xlv (same series vs XLV) and umcsent_spy (the expected-business-conditions diffusion vs SPY).

data_provenance.source: FRED / ALFRED (University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers)
